To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
low current microelectrodes can excite a wide range of neuronal elements, which are not necessarily close to the electrode tip.
low current stimulation activates the axon initial segments and thin axons and that dendrites with diameters smaller than 1 μm can be activated.
the axon initial segments are the most excitable structures of the mammalian nervous system followed by small diameter axons and dendritic branches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most probable spike initiation sites for low current stimulation.
the question of whether low current stimulation is capable to selectively activate certain cell bodies or whether it rather excites the entire neural axis.
the identification of the spike initiation site for low current stimulation of the mammalian CNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spike initiation is not a single event but depends on the electrode configuration, the fiber size, and the electrode-fiber distance.
the axon initial section and thin axons are most excitable.
the axon initial segments are most sensitive to stimulation, followed by thin axons and thin dendrites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cathodic stimulation activates the neural tissue by a combination of direct excitation, intracellular current flow and activation of the AIS.
the AIS is the most probable site for cathodic stimulation, but the probability decreases with increasing distance from the electrode.
the AIS is the most probable spike initiation site, but the probability of dendritic spikes increases with electrode-fiber distance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the axon initial segments (AIS) of pyramidal cells in layer 5 are the most likely site for low current stimulation in the mammalian cortex, but other locations, especially dendrites, can also be excited.
low current stimulation of the cortex is likely to excite the AIS and thin axons and that the axon and soma are not the only candidates for spike initiation.
the AIS is not the only spike initiation site in mammalian cortex.
